subject: TerraHealth order form — redlines on pricing ladder, min-commit and invoicing path
messages:
From: James Allen <james.allen@terrahealth.io>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Sylvia Cho <sylvia.cho@terrahealth.io>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Redlines on Order Form v3 (TerraHealth)

Hi Priya / Kimberly,

Thanks for the run-through on the demo yesterday — team was impressed. Attached is our procurement team's redline (Terra_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf). High level asks:
- Push net terms to Net 45 from Net 30 (standard for our finance).
- Split invoicing: three tranches aligned to commitments rather than a single upfront invoice.
- Request evidence of tax residency for Redwood entity billing (we need W-8/W-9 copy).
- We left comments on the min-commit ramp: prefer a 3-quarter staircase instead of the two-step in v2.

Can your legal/finance folks review and confirm what you can accept? We're aiming for Procurement exec approval next week.

Thanks,
James Allen
Director, Procurement
TerraHealth Inc.

Subject: Re: Redlines on Order Form v3 (TerraHealth)

James — thanks for sending this over and for the candid asks. Looping Ben (sales lead) to keep commercial visibility.

Quick notes while we pull in Legal:
- Net 45: we can consider Net 45 for established customers on a reserved capacity agreement, but need approval from Finance for any change to standard Net 30 on first purchase. Ben, can you confirm whether we have account-level flexibility here for RH-4721-TERRA?
- Tranche invoicing: open to phasing invoices by commitment milestones; need to map exact milestone dates to billing triggers so accounting can plan cashflow.
- Tax residency: we will provide Redwood's W-9 and entity billing details (see below) — legal requires the order form to reference billing entity explicitly.
- Min-commit ramp: Kimberly and Karthik — can you prepare proposed redline language for a 3-quarter staircase and highlight any pricing impact?

Action items: 
1) Kimberly/Karthik — internal redline with clause language and pricing delta by EOD Monday.
2) Ben — check Finance/Revenue policy on Net 45 exceptions and confirm tolerances.
3) Priya (me) — after your inputs, I'll consolidate and send a single redline back to James.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: TerraHealth order form — proposed redline language

Priya / Ben / Karthik — internal note before we reply-all to TerraHealth. I pulled Legal into a quick sync and have preliminary text below. I focused on the three commercial points James flagged.

1) Net terms (Net 45 request)
Proposed: "Customer shall pay invoices within thirty (30) days of receipt, except where Customer executes a written payment schedule ("Payment Schedule") signed by both parties that specifies Net 45 terms for specified invoices. Redwood may require credit approval or an upfront partial payment as a condition of granting Net 45 terms for an initial term."
Rationale: preserves standard Net 30 while giving a path for negotiated Net 45 tied to credit checks; reduces Finance exposure.

2) Tranche invoicing by commitment milestones
Proposed: add SOW table mapping milestone percentages to invoice triggers, e.g., 30% at commencement, 40% at attainment of Q2 commit threshold, 30% on final acceptance or quarterly reconciliation. Require PO referencing order form.
Rationale: Makes cashflow predictable and ties invoicing to measurable commit events. Accounting asked that any tranche schedule include explicit due dates +/- tolerance window.

3) Min-commit staircase
Proposed: replace two-step with three-step ladder: Q1 40%, Q2 30%, Q3 30% of annual committed units; include price per unit for each tranche and a reconciliation clause for over/under consumption at year-end.
Rationale: Aligns with TerraHealth's ask while protecting Redwood pricing. We should calculate the pricing delta (estimated +4% on effective rate) and surface to Ben.

Open asks for TerraHealth that Legal needs before final: billing entity (legal name and tax ID), remit address, preferred PO number format, and whether TerraHealth requires us to use their in-country entity for EU VAT handling.

I'll draft a short redline (one-page summary) and an updated PDF redline to attach. Priya — if Ben can confirm Net 45 guardrails, I can finalize wording Monday.

Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: TerraHealth order form — redlines, summary and next steps

James / Sylvia — thanks for the patience while we coordinated internally. Attached is a concise summary of Redwood's commercial redlines and the updated PDF with comments (RH-orderform-redline-summary-20261123.xlsx and Terra_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf). Highlights: 
- Net terms: Redwood proposes the Payment Schedule approach (Net 30 default; Net 45 available via signed Payment Schedule subject to credit approval).
- Invoicing: Proposed tranche schedule in the summary (30/40/30) with billing triggers tied to commit attainment; please confirm whether you prefer milestone dates or percentage attainment triggers.
- Min-commit staircase: proposed 3-quarter ladder included; estimated effective pricing delta ~+4% to preserve economics.

Next steps suggested: 
1) TerraFinance to confirm billing entity, tax ID and remit address so Legal can prepare the Payment Schedule template and W-9/W-8 as needed.
2) TerraHealth to confirm PO timing and whether they will provide a single PO per tranche or an umbrella PO referencing the order form.
3) If acceptable, I'll send the consolidated redline PDF and a DocuSign link for the Payment Schedule (we can attach to the Order Form).

James — are you available for a 30-minute call Wednesday to close commercial points? If so, propose 10:00–10:30 PT.

Thanks all —
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
(priya.natarajan@redwood.com)
